stories.title: Zverev Dominates de Minaur to Reach Shanghai Semifinals

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text: Zverev into the Shanghai semis. De Minaur didn't get a look — 6-4, 6-4 in under 80 minutes. Top seed through in straight sets despite the ankle issues. He meets Davidovich Fokina in the SF. #ShanghaiMasters #Tennis

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text: Zverev vs. Davidovich Fokina. That's your first Shanghai semifinal. Zverev looks sharp — de Minaur couldn't break him once. Year-end No. 1 is playing like year-end No. 1. #ShanghaiMasters #Tennis

facebook.long_form:
Window: 10:30 AM ET

Alexander Zverev is in the Shanghai Masters semifinals — and he made it look easy.

The world No. 1 dismantled Alex de Minaur 6-4, 6-4 in the quarterfinals on Thursday, barely breaking a sweat in a match that lasted under 80 minutes. De Minaur had arrived in the quarterfinals without dropping a set or a service game all week. Against Zverev, none of that mattered.

Zverev broke de Minaur once in each set and never once faced a break point himself. It was the kind of dominant, professional performance that reminds you why he's the No. 1 player in the world — and why the ankle issues that have been whispered about all week haven't slowed him down.

He now faces Alejandro Davidovich Fokina in the semifinals on Saturday. Fokina advanced when Arthur Gea retired injured in the quarterfinals.

Zverev is two wins away from the Shanghai title.
facebook.image_caption:
Window: 12:30 PM ET

Zverev through to the Shanghai semis. 6-4, 6-4 over de Minaur. Dominant, efficient, and ankle issues or not — he looks very much like a champion this week. 🎾

article.headline: Zverev Crushes de Minaur in Under 80 Minutes to Reach Shanghai Semifinals

stories.title: Ann Li Ends Sabalenka's Legendary Wuhan Winning Streak

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text: ANN LI BEATS ARYNA SABALENKA IN WUHAN. 3-6, 6-4, 7-6(5). 10 match points. 9 saves by Sabalenka. One of the biggest WTA upsets of 2026. The Wuhan winning streak — over. #WuhanOpen #Tennis

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text: Sabalenka had never lost in Wuhan. Three titles. Back to 2018. Ann Li ends it — on the 10th match point. The streak that seemed unbreakable is over. What a result. #WuhanOpen #Tennis

facebook.long_form:
Window: 8:00 AM ET

This is the kind of result that will be talked about for years.

Ann Li, an American ranked outside the top 50, has just ended Aryna Sabalenka's legendary unbeaten run in Wuhan — winning 3-6, 6-4, 7-6(5) in one of the most dramatic matches of the 2026 WTA season.

The match had everything. Sabalenka won the first set and looked in control. Li clawed back the second. In the third, Sabalenka served for it, saved nine match points, and pushed the tiebreak to the edge. But on the 10th match point, Li got through.

Sabalenka received a right knee medical timeout and committed 44 unforced errors — unusual for the normally composed Belarusian. Her Wuhan record had been one of tennis' most remarkable statistics: three titles (2018, 2019, 2024), not a single loss at the venue since her first title eight years ago.

It's over now. Ann Li's biggest career win. One of the great upset stories of the 2026 WTA season.
facebook.image_caption:
Window: 3:00 PM ET

Ten match points. Nine saves. On the tenth — Ann Li beats Aryna Sabalenka in Wuhan. The three-time champion's unbeaten streak at this venue is gone. What a result. 🎾

article.headline: Ann Li Stuns Sabalenka on 10th Match Point, Ending the Legend of Wuhan's Unbeatable Champion

stories.title: Gea's Shanghai Dream Ends With Injury Retirement

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text: Arthur Gea's Shanghai run is over — but not how anyone wanted. He retired after 22 minutes against Davidovich Fokina, right leg injury, trailing 4-1. Beat Shelton. Beat Mensik. A star in the making. #ShanghaiMasters

facebook.long_form:
Window: 12:30 PM ET

Arthur Gea's Shanghai Masters run is over — and it ended in a way that no one wanted.

The 21-year-old Frenchman retired from his quarterfinal match against Alejandro Davidovich Fokina after just 22 minutes, citing a right leg injury. He was trailing 4-1 in the first set when he had to stop.

It was a heartbreaking end to what had been one of the stories of the tournament. Gea had beaten Ben Shelton in a two-set thriller, then upset 13th seed Jakub Mensik to reach his first-ever Masters 1000 quarterfinal. In a draw full of stars, the young Frenchman had made his own noise.

He'll be back. But Thursday was not his day.

Davidovich Fokina advances to the semifinals, where he'll face top seed Zverev.
facebook.image_caption:
Window: 3:00 PM ET

Gea's run ends in the worst way — a right leg injury, 22 minutes, trailing 4-1. He beat Shelton. He beat Mensik. He was here. A star in the making. 💙

article.headline: Gea's Shanghai Dream Ends in Heartbreak as Injury Forces Retirement in Quarterfinal

stories.title: Shanghai Semifinal Preview — Zverev vs. Davidovich Fokina, Plus Oct 16 QFs

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text: Shanghai semifinals taking shape. Zverev vs. Davidovich Fokina is confirmed. Medvedev vs. Paul and Ruud vs. Jodar decide the other semi on Friday. The last four in Shanghai is no sure thing. #ShanghaiMasters

facebook.long_form:
Window: 3:00 PM ET

The Shanghai Masters is taking shape — and it's shaping up to be a proper semifinal weekend.

Two spots are already confirmed: Alexander Zverev (No. 1) takes on Alejandro Davidovich Fokina in one semifinal. Zverev has been the dominant player of the tournament; Fokina advances after Arthur Gea's injury retirement.

Two spots are still up for grabs on Friday (October 16): Daniil Medvedev vs. Tommy Paul, and Rafael Jodar vs. Casper Ruud. Paul has been one of the most consistent ATP performers this year — he's reached the quarterfinals at all six ATP Masters 1000 hard-court events in 2026. Medvedev, coming off his QF against Tsitsipas, will be the favorite.

Jodar vs. Ruud is less predictable. The young Spaniard has had a breakthrough Shanghai, while Ruud has been quietly making his way through the draw.

The semifinals run on Saturday. Whoever is left will battle for the Shanghai title on Sunday.
facebook.image_caption:
Window: 6:00 PM ET

Zverev vs. Davidovich Fokina. Medvedev vs. Paul. Ruud vs. Jodar. The last eight in Shanghai is nearly resolved — and the semifinals are going to be worth watching. 🎾

stories.title: Wuhan QF Field Set — Swiatek, Ostapenko, Chwalinska in the Mix

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: Wuhan QF watch: Ann Li is in (beat Sabalenka). Ostapenko is in (beat Fernandez, had beaten Pegula). Chwalinska is in (upset Jovic — her first WTA 1000 QF). Swiatek on deck. This draw is wide open. #WuhanOpen

facebook.long_form:
Window: 6:00 PM ET

The Wuhan Open quarterfinals are arriving — and the draw has been blown wide open.

The biggest news: Ann Li is in the quarterfinals after ending Sabalenka's legendary Wuhan winning streak. She faces Janice Tjen next.

Jelena Ostapenko has been on a tear — she first beat No. 2 seed Jessica Pegula (saving three match points), then knocked out Leylah Fernandez 6-1, 1-6, 6-4 to reach her first Wuhan QF in nine years.

Maja Chwalinska is also there — the 16th seed upset world No. 11 Iva Jovic 6-4, 6-1 in her first-ever WTA 1000 quarterfinal appearance.

Maria Sakkari and Elina Svitolina advanced in straight sets and are both in the mix.

And Iga Swiatek, the last WTA Finals hopeful among the top seeds still standing, is closing in on a quarterfinal berth.

This Wuhan draw is no longer Sabalenka's to lose. It's anyone's.
facebook.image_caption:
Window: 9:00 PM ET

Wuhan QF field: Ann Li. Ostapenko. Chwalinska. Sakkari. Svitolina. Swiatek incoming. After Sabalenka's exit — this tournament is wide open. 🎾

article.headline: Wuhan Open QF Field: Sabalenka Out, Ann Li In, and a Tournament Wide Open
